answer: Identity can rest on a rented postal box backed by a year of utility bills. The applicant shows a post-office rental contract plus twelve months of bills delivered to that same box, all in one name. A farm would need a separate rented box and a full year of real bills for every copy, paying rent and waiting, while one honest agent just renews the box they already hold. The dune of forged paperwork keeps growing for the faker, the pigment on each bill is a dated stamp that cannot be backdated, and the terrace of cost stays flat for the real resident.
